stem: Which of these costs is included in the cost of a machine under IAS 16?

options.content: Installation costs needed to bring the machine into use
options.rationale: Correct: directly attributable cost of bringing the asset to working condition.

options.content: Training of the staff who will operate it
options.rationale: Training is an expense of the period.

options.content: The first year's insurance of the machine
options.rationale: Running costs are expenses, not part of cost.

options.content: General administration costs of the head office
options.rationale: Administration costs are not directly attributable.

explanation: Cost includes the purchase price (less trade discounts) and directly attributable costs such as delivery, installation and testing.

stem: A business adds an extra floor to its factory building in Bulawayo. How is the expenditure treated?

options.content: Capital expenditure, added to the cost of the building
options.rationale: Correct: it increases the future benefits of the asset.

options.content: Revenue expenditure, charged to the statement of profit or loss
options.rationale: Repairs and maintenance are revenue expenditure; an extension is not.

options.content: Capital expenditure, charged to a repairs account
options.rationale: Capital expenditure is added to the asset account.

options.content: Drawings, because the owner benefits
options.rationale: It is a business expense on an asset, not private use.

explanation: Expenditure that enlarges or improves an asset (or extends its life) is capitalised; repairs that merely maintain it are expenses.

stem: Under the revaluation model of IAS 16, at what amount is an asset carried after a revaluation?

options.content: Historical cost less accumulated depreciation, whatever its current value
options.rationale: That is the cost model.

options.content: Its original purchase price, with no deduction for depreciation
options.rationale: Under neither model is it carried at original cost without depreciation.

options.content: Net realisable value at the revaluation date less selling costs
options.rationale: NRV is a different valuation basis.

options.content: Fair value at the date of revaluation less any later accumulated depreciation
options.rationale: Correct.

explanation: The revaluation model uses fair value at the revaluation date, then deducts depreciation on the revalued amount.

stem: Where is a surplus on the revaluation of a building recorded?

options.content: In the statement of profit or loss as other income
options.rationale: An unrealised surplus is not recognised in profit.

options.content: In a revaluation reserve in equity
options.rationale: Correct: it is not profit.

options.content: As a liability until the building is sold
options.rationale: A surplus is part of equity.

options.content: As a reduction in the accumulated depreciation only
options.rationale: Accumulated depreciation is eliminated, but the surplus is credited to a reserve.

explanation: An increase in carrying amount on revaluation is credited to the revaluation reserve, so profit is not affected.

stem: Tendai's premises have a cost of US\$150,000 and accumulated depreciation of US\$45,000. They are revalued at US\$190,000. What is the revaluation surplus?

options.rationale: This ignores accumulated depreciation, which is part of the carrying amount.
The accumulated depreciation is not deducted from the valuation.
This is the valuation, not the surplus.

stem: After an upward revaluation of a building, what is the effect on the annual depreciation charge and on profit?

options.content: The depreciation charge decreases and profit for the year increases
options.rationale: A higher carrying amount gives a higher charge, not lower.

options.content: The depreciation charge increases and profit for the year decreases
options.rationale: Correct: depreciation is based on the higher revalued amount.

options.content: The depreciation charge is unchanged because the useful life is unchanged
options.rationale: Depreciation is calculated on the revalued amount, so it rises.

options.content: The depreciation charge increases and profit for the year increases
options.rationale: Higher depreciation reduces profit.

explanation: The new, higher valuation is depreciated over the remaining life, so the charge rises and profit falls.
hints: Depreciation is a share of the (new) carrying amount over the remaining life.

stem: Which valuation basis is most suitable for a business that is about to close down and sell all its assets?

options.content: Historical cost
options.rationale: Historical cost shows what was paid, not what will be received.

options.content: Replacement cost
options.rationale: Replacement cost assumes assets will be replaced and the business continues.

options.content: Net realisable (exit) value
options.rationale: Correct: it shows what the assets will fetch.

options.content: Cost less accumulated depreciation
options.rationale: This is the carrying amount under the cost model, for a continuing business.

explanation: A closing business is concerned with the amounts that can be realised from sale.
hints: Will the business continue to use the assets?

stem: A piece of land has a revaluation reserve of US\$4,000 from an earlier upward revaluation of the same land. It is now revalued downwards by US\$7,500. How is the decrease treated?

options.content: The whole US\$7,500 as an expense in profit or loss
options.rationale: The existing reserve on that land must be used first.

options.content: The whole US\$7,500 to the revaluation reserve
options.rationale: The reserve cannot go negative; the excess goes to profit or loss.

options.content: US\$4,000 to the revaluation reserve and US\$3,500 to profit or loss
options.rationale: Correct: reserve first, excess to profit or loss.

options.content: US\$4,000 to profit or loss and US\$3,500 to the revaluation reserve
options.rationale: The order is reversed.

explanation: A decrease is first set against the revaluation reserve on the same asset; any excess (7,500 − 4,000 = 3,500) is charged to profit or loss.
hints: The earlier surplus on that asset is reversed first.

stem: Under the revaluation model, a business may revalue just one building and leave other buildings at cost.
explanation: False. If one asset is revalued, all assets in the same class must be revalued.
hints: Think about the class of assets.

stem: A revaluation surplus is part of the profit for the year.
explanation: False. It is recorded in the revaluation reserve in equity.

stem: Match each valuation basis to its description.

right.content: The amount that would be received on sale, less selling costs
Fair value at the revaluation date less later depreciation
The amount paid when the asset was acquired
What it would cost now to buy a similar asset

explanation: These are the bases examined in this topic.

stem: Complete the statements.

payload.template: Under the cost model, carrying amount = cost less {{blank:a}}. A revaluation surplus is credited to the {{blank:b}}.

explanation: The cost model deducts accumulated depreciation; a surplus goes to equity, not profit.

stem: Sipho buys a baking machine. The invoice price is US\$28,500 less a 10% trade discount. He pays US\$800 for delivery, US\$1,150 for installation and US\$600 to train the bakers. At what amount is the machine recorded in the asset account?
explanation: Net price 28,500 × 90% = 25,650. Cost = 25,650 + 800 + 1,150 = 27,600. Training (600) is an expense. Ignoring the discount gives 30,450; including training gives 28,200.
workedSolution: 1. Net price 28,500 × 90% = 25,650. Cost = 25,650 + 800 + 1,150 = 27,600. Training (600) is an expense. Ignoring the discount gives 30,450; including training gives 28,200.
hints: Which of these costs bring the machine to working condition?

stem: A warehouse in Masvingo cost US\$120,000 and was depreciated over 40 years using the straight-line method. After some years it was revalued to US\$180,000, with 30 years of useful life remaining and the accumulated depreciation eliminated. Calculate the annual depreciation charge after the revaluation.
explanation: 180,000 ÷ 30 = 6,000 a year. The previous charge was 120,000 ÷ 40 = 3,000.
workedSolution: 1. 180,000 ÷ 30 = 6,000 a year. The previous charge was 120,000 ÷ 40 = 3,000.
hints: Depreciate the revalued amount over the remaining life.

stem: Chipo's land has a revaluation reserve of US\$12,000 created by an earlier increase in its value. The land is now revalued downwards by US\$20,000. What amount is charged to the statement of profit or loss?
explanation: The first 12,000 of the decrease is charged to the reserve. The excess, 20,000 − 12,000 = 8,000, is an expense in profit or loss.
workedSolution: 1. The first 12,000 of the decrease is charged to the reserve. The excess, 20,000 − 12,000 = 8,000, is an expense in profit or loss.

stem: Nyasha revalues her factory building to US\$240,000 on 1 January and eliminates the accumulated depreciation. The remaining useful life is 20 years and she uses the straight-line method. Calculate the carrying amount of the building at the end of that year.
hints: Charge one year's depreciation on the revalued amount.

stem: Name the reserve credited when a non-current asset is revalued upwards.
explanation: The surplus is credited to the revaluation reserve (a capital reserve, not profit).

stem: Distinguish between the cost model and the revaluation model of IAS 16.

points.description: Cost model: asset carried at cost less accumulated depreciation
Cost model: the carrying amount can fall well below current value when prices rise
Revaluation model: asset carried at fair value at the revaluation date less later depreciation
Revaluation model: increases are credited to a revaluation reserve and the whole class must be revalued

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Under the cost model an asset is carried at its cost less accumulated depreciation, which may be far below its present value. Under the revaluation model it is carried at fair value at the date of revaluation less later depreciation; the surplus goes to a revaluation reserve and every asset in the class must be revalued.

explanation: Give the measurement basis and one consequence for each model.

stem: Explain why the cost of staff training is not included in the cost of a new machine.

points.description: Cost includes only expenditure needed to bring the asset to working condition
Training benefits the staff and is not part of the asset itself
It is an expense of the period charged to profit or loss

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Cost is limited to the purchase price and costs of bringing the machine to working condition, such as delivery and installation. Training does not create part of the machine, so it is charged to profit or loss as an expense.

explanation: Link the definition of cost to the nature of training.
hints: Is the training part of the machine?

stem: Evaluate whether a company that owns several office blocks in a period of rising property prices should adopt the revaluation model.

points.description: Benefit: statement of financial position shows assets nearer to current value
Benefit: equity and net assets rise, which may help the business to borrow
Drawback: valuations cost money and are subjective, and must be kept up to date
Drawback: higher depreciation reduces profit; a justified conclusion is given

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The revaluation model would show the offices at a value nearer to the market and strengthen equity, which may help the company to borrow. However, regular valuations cost money and are subjective, and the higher depreciation lowers profit. Because prices are rising and property is a large part of the company's assets, the model is probably worthwhile if the cost of valuation is acceptable.

explanation: A balanced judgement weighs the more realistic carrying amount against cost and subjectivity.
hints: One benefit, one drawback, then a judgement.

stem: Tatenda's company owns a commercial building in Masvingo. On 1 January 2026 its cost was US\$360,000 and the accumulated depreciation was US\$90,000. The directors adopt the revaluation model and a professional valuer values the building at US\$420,000. The remaining useful life is 30 years and depreciation is straight line. The year end is 31 December.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the carrying amount of the building before the revaluation.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Prepare the journal entry to record the revaluation. A narrative is required.

points.description: Debit provision for depreciation 90,000
Credit revaluation reserve 150,000
Date and narrative

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Journal**

| Date | Details | Debit US\$ | Credit US\$ |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 Jan 2026 | Provision for depreciation: buildings | 90,000 |  |
|  | Buildings at cost / valuation | 60,000 |  |
|  | Revaluation reserve |  | 150,000 |
|  | *Revaluation of buildings to 420,000; accumulated depreciation eliminated* |  |  |

parts.explanation: The accumulated depreciation is eliminated and the building is restated to the valuation.

parts.label: (d)
parts.explanation: Depreciation is on the revalued amount: 420,000 ÷ 30 = 14,000.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Depreciation is on the revalued amount: 420,000 ÷ 30 = 14,000.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Explain how the revaluation affects the profit for 2026.

points.description: The surplus is not profit, so it does not increase profit
Depreciation is higher on the revalued amount, so profit is lower

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The surplus is credited to the revaluation reserve, so profit does not increase. The depreciation charge is higher than before because it is based on the higher valuation, so profit for 2026 is lower.

parts.explanation: The revaluation reduces profit through higher depreciation.

explanation: This item practises a revaluation: surplus, journal and the effect on depreciation.
hints: The accumulated depreciation is eliminated on revaluation.
Depreciate the revalued amount over the remaining life.

stem: Thandeka's bakery in Gweru bought a new industrial mixer on 1 March 2026. The invoice price was US\$64,000. She also paid: import duty US\$3,200, delivery US\$1,900, installation US\$2,400, professional fees for certifying the installation US\$800, a repair of the old mixer US\$1,200 and training of bakers US\$1,500.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Is each item part of the cost of the new mixer?

parts.label: (i)
parts.explanation: Yes. Import duties are a non-refundable cost of acquisition.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.explanation: No. It relates to a different asset and is revenue expenditure.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.explanation: No. Training is not a cost of bringing the mixer to working condition.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.stem: Professional fees for certifying the installation
parts.explanation: Yes. Fees directly attributable to bringing the asset into use are part of its cost.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the amount at which the mixer is recorded in the asset account.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Thandeka is considering valuing her premises at replacement cost in the statement of financial position instead of historical cost. Evaluate this suggestion.

points.description: Replacement cost shows the current cost of a similar asset, which is more relevant when prices have risen
Historical cost is objective and verifiable
Replacement cost needs estimates and professional valuation, which is subjective and costly
Justified conclusion, for example that the revaluation model with regular valuations is a sensible compromise

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Replacement cost shows what a similar asset would cost now, so it may be more relevant when prices have risen. Historical cost is objective and checked against invoices. Replacement cost needs estimates and valuation, which is costly and subjective. A sensible compromise is to use the revaluation model with regular professional valuations.

parts.explanation: A balanced answer weighs relevance against reliability.

explanation: This item practises the cost of a new asset and the choice between valuation bases.
hints: Only costs of bringing the asset into working condition are capitalised.
Evaluate: one advantage, one disadvantage, then a conclusion.
